key_insight: The paper derives a joint loss characterization for learning rate and batch size, enabling a closed-form optimal batch size schedule that improves training over static batching.
engineering_relevance: For large-scale model training, this suggests batch size should be scheduled dynamically alongside the learning rate rather than held fixed.
method: Model deep learning training through convex optimization dynamics.
Derive a joint characterization of loss as a function of learning-rate and batch-size schedules.
Use the characterization to compute a closed-form optimal batch-size schedule for any chosen learning-rate schedule.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the resulting joint scaling laws consistently outperform static batch-size baselines.
watch_item: Practical gains may depend on accurately matching the assumed optimizer/dynamics and on the implementation complexity of changing batch size during training.
paper_title: Towards joint scaling laws with optimal batch size schedules
